conn.title: Connect your streaming software
conn.subtitle: Only once, it takes 2 minutes. VirtualDeck then reconnects by itself whenever your software is open.
conn.followSteps: Follow the steps below, then click “Connect”.
conn.error.auth.obs.missing: OBS asks for a password: copy it from “Show Connect Info” (step 3).
conn.error.auth.obs.wrong: OBS rejected the password. Copy it again from “Show Connect Info” (step 3).
conn.error.auth.streamlabs.missing: Streamlabs asks for the API token: copy it from the Remote Control settings (step 3).
conn.error.auth.streamlabs.wrong: Streamlabs rejected the token. Copy it again from the Remote Control settings (step 3).
conn.error.unreachable.obs: OBS is not responding. Check that it is open and that the WebSocket server is enabled (step 2). Retrying every 5 seconds.
conn.error.unreachable.streamlabs: Streamlabs is not responding. Check that it is open and that Remote Control is enabled (step 2). Retrying every 5 seconds.
guide.obs.title: Set up OBS Studio
guide.obs.s1.title: Check your OBS version
guide.obs.s1.body: The WebSocket server is built into OBS since version 28. Check yours in Help → About. If it is older, install the latest one from obsproject.com.
guide.obs.s2.title: Enable the WebSocket server
guide.obs.s2.body: In OBS, open Tools → WebSocket Server Settings and tick Enable WebSocket server. Leave the port on 4455.
guide.obs.s3.title: Copy the password
guide.obs.s3.body: If Enable Authentication is ticked (recommended), click Show Connect Info and then Copy next to the server password.
guide.sl.title: Set up Streamlabs Desktop
guide.sl.s1.title: Open the Remote Control settings
guide.sl.s1.body: In Streamlabs Desktop, open Settings → Remote Control.
guide.sl.s2.title: Show the connection details
guide.sl.s2.body: Click the QR code to reveal it, then click Show details. Leave the port on 59650.
guide.sl.s3.title: Copy the API token
guide.sl.s3.body: Copy the API Token shown in the details. Never share it: it gives full control over your Streamlabs.
guide.connect.title: Paste it here and connect
guide.connect.body: Paste it into the field above and click Connect. When the dot turns green, you're done: your scene and source names will appear in the Buttons tab.
guide.anim.title: Create an “animation” button
guide.anim.s1.title: Add the video to your scene
guide.anim.s1.body: In your streaming software, add a Media Source to your scene and pick your video (ideally a .webm with a transparent background). Tick Restart playback when source becomes active and leave Loop unticked.
guide.anim.s2.title: Hide the source
guide.anim.s2.body: Click the eye icon next to the source to hide it. The button will make it appear.
guide.anim.s3.title: Set up the button
guide.anim.s3.body: In the Buttons tab, choose the Source / animation action, pick your source, keep the Animation behavior and set the duration to the length of your video. The source shows up, plays, then hides by itself.
faq.title: Not working?
faq.offline.a: Check that your streaming software is open and that remote control is enabled (step 2). Default addresses: ws://127.0.0.1:4455 for OBS, ws://127.0.0.1:59650/api/websocket for Streamlabs.
faq.auth.a: Copy it again from your software (step 3). If you generated a new password or token there, the old one no longer works: paste the new one here.
faq.remote.q: My streaming software runs on another PC
faq.remote.a: Replace 127.0.0.1 with the IP address of that PC, and allow your streaming software through the Windows firewall over there.
faq.scene.a: The name must match exactly (capitals, spaces, accents). Once connected, pick the scene from the suggested list instead of typing it.

settings.hotkeyHint: Click, then press your combination. F13 to F24 keys (programmable mice or keyboards) also work on their own.

settings.closeAfterHint: Otherwise it stays open until Esc or a click outside.
settings.closeOutside: Close the deck when clicking outside
settings.closeOutsideHint: Off, it stays open until Esc, its hotkey or an action.
settings.loginHint: The app starts quietly in the notification area.
backup.title: Backup
backup.exportHint: Creates a file with your buttons, their sounds and their images. Handy to move to a new PC or share your deck. Connection passwords and tokens are not included.
backup.importHint: Replaces your buttons, grid and shortcut. Your connection settings are kept.
backup.importQuestion: Replace your buttons with the ones from “{file}”?
backup.importDetail: Your grid and shortcut will be replaced too. Your connection settings are kept.
backup.importOpenWarning: {count} button(s) open a program or a link, or type on the keyboard: check them in the editor before using them.
backup.exportMissing: {count} missing file(s) could not be included: {files}.
backup.importedHotkeyTaken: Setup imported, but the shortcut “{hotkey}” is already taken: pick another one above.
update.installTitle: Downloads the new version, installs it and restarts VirtualDeck. Your keys and settings are kept.
update.failed: The update could not be downloaded (connection lost or damaged file). Try again in a moment.
update.done: VirtualDeck has been updated to version {version}.
field.verticalMissing: Aitum Vertical plugin not found in OBS: only the horizontal part of this button will work.
error.verticalMissing: Aitum Vertical plugin not found in OBS.
error.verticalUnsupported: Vertical scenes only work with OBS and the Aitum Vertical plugin.
field.horizontalPlaceholder: Empty: the horizontal scene doesn't change
field.verticalPlaceholder: Empty: the vertical scene doesn't change
field.verticalSourcesHint: Sources of vertical scenes require OBS 32 or later.
error.verticalSourcesObs32: Sources of vertical scenes require OBS 32 or later.
settings.deckPositionCursor: The deck opens under the mouse. Drag it by its top bar to pin it somewhere.
settings.deckPositionSaved: The deck always opens where you moved it.
field.horizontalSourcePlaceholder: Empty: nothing animates on the horizontal canvas
field.verticalSourcePlaceholder: Empty: nothing animates on the vertical canvas
deck.verticalIssueHint: {count} button(s) use the vertical canvas, but the Aitum Vertical plugin isn't found in OBS: they only change the horizontal part.
deck.verticalIssueKey: Aitum Vertical plugin not found: only the horizontal part of this button works.
settings.deckScaleHint: You can also drag the bottom-right corner of the deck.
deck.resize: Drag to enlarge or shrink the deck
action.obs-replay.hint: Saves the last seconds to a video file, while streaming, recording or neither. The replay buffer must be running in {software} (in OBS: “Start Replay Buffer” button, once enabled in Settings › Output).
field.muteHint: The button shows “MUTED” in red while this audio is muted.
field.replayVerticalHint: The vertical clip uses Aitum Vertical's Backtrack, which must be running.
error.replayDisabled: The replay buffer isn't enabled in {software}. In OBS: Settings › Output › Replay Buffer.
field.outputHint: Horizontal: the regular {software} output. Vertical: the Aitum Vertical plugin output (TikTok, Shorts…).
field.keyHotkeyHint: Runs this button from anywhere, without opening the deck. F13 to F24 keys work on their own.
field.keyHotkeyTaken: This hotkey is already used (by another app, the deck or another button): pick another one.
action.multi.hint: Runs several actions in order, with an optional wait before each one. If a step fails, the next ones still run.
action.page.hint: Changes the deck's page, without closing it. With its hotkey, this button opens the deck on that page.
page.removeConfirm: Delete page "{name}" and all its buttons?
undo.hint: Ctrl + Z undoes too, and Ctrl + Y redoes.
page.name: Name
settings.pageModeHint: “In the deck” swaps the grid. “Deck on top” opens the page in a bubble coming out of the button, above the deck; closing the deck then goes back to page 1.
phone.title: Phone
phone.enable: Use my phone as a deck
phone.enableHint: The phone must be on the same Wi-Fi as this PC. Nothing is opened to the internet, and only a phone that scanned the QR code can use it.
phone.noNetwork: No local network found: connect the PC to your router (Wi-Fi or cable).
phone.qrHint: Scan it with the phone's camera, then add the page to the home screen to open it like an app.
phone.qrWarning: Keep this QR code to yourself (avoid showing it on stream): it lets a device control your deck, but only one connected to your Wi-Fi.
phone.firewallHint: If Windows asks for permission for VirtualDeck, allow it for your home network's type (shown in Settings › Network & internet): that is what lets your phone connect.
phone.newKeyHint: Creates a new QR code: phones already paired will need to scan it again.
phone.newKeyConfirm: Disconnect all phones? They will need to scan the new QR code.
phone.pairHint: On the PC, open VirtualDeck › Settings › Phone, show the QR code and scan it.
phone.blocked: Too many refused attempts: try again in 10 minutes.
phone.maxPhonesHint: Places taken: {count} of {max}. The first devices that scan the QR code take them; the next ones are refused. "New QR code" frees the places.
phone.maxPhonesNone: Every device that scans the QR code can use the deck.
phone.fullHint: This deck already accepts the maximum number of phones. On the PC, in Settings › Phone, raise the limit or create a new QR code.
field.appIconNone: No icon found: pick the program (.exe) or its shortcut with Browse…
page.full: Page "{name}" has no free spot left
lights.title: Connected lights
lights.hueHint: Control your Hue lights through the home bridge. While off, VirtualDeck never contacts the bridge.
lights.goveeHint: Control your Wi-Fi Govee lights ("LAN Control" on in the Govee Home app). While off, no search is sent on the network.
lights.hueOff: Philips Hue lights are turned off in the settings.
lights.goveeOff: Govee lights are turned off in the settings.
hue.bridgeHint: Link your Hue bridge to turn your lights on, off or change their mood from a key. Everything stays on your home network, no Hue account needed.
hue.manualHint: Bridge not listed? Enter its address (Hue app › Settings › Hue Bridges).
hue.noneFound: No bridge found. Check that it is plugged in and on the same network as this PC, or enter its address (Hue app › Settings › Hue Bridges).
hue.pressButton: Press the round button in the middle of the bridge… ({seconds} s)
hue.timeout: The bridge button was not pressed in time. Click "Link" and try again.
hue.pairedNow: Bridge linked: you can now create "Hue lights" keys.
hue.pairedHint: Address {ip}. Hue keys work while this PC is on the same network as the bridge.
hue.toggleHint: When off, the lights turn on with these settings; when on, they turn off.
hue.notPairedCallout: No Hue bridge is linked yet.
hueError.unreachable: The Hue bridge does not answer. Check that it is plugged in and that this PC is on the same network.
hueError.certificate: The device at the bridge address is not the same anymore. Link your bridge again in the settings.
hueError.notPaired: No Hue bridge is linked: link it in the settings.
hueError.unauthorized: The Hue bridge no longer knows VirtualDeck: link it again in the settings.
hueError.notFound: This light or scene no longer exists on the Hue bridge.
hueError.address: This address is not on your home network.
hueError.notBridge: No Hue bridge answers at this address.
hueError.linkButton: Press the bridge button, then try again.
hueError.bridge: The Hue bridge returned an error: {detail}
govee.lanHint: A light is missing? In the Govee Home app, open it › Settings and turn on "LAN Control". It must be on the same network as this PC.
govee.noneFound: No Govee light found. In the Govee Home app, open your light › Settings and turn on "LAN Control". It must be on the same network as this PC.
goveeError.notFound: The Govee light does not answer. Check that it is plugged in, on the same network as this PC, with "LAN Control" on in the Govee Home app.
goveeError.port: Another program is using the Govee lights port (4002). Close it, then try again.
goveeError.noStatus: The Govee light did not give its state: try again, or use a "Turn on" or "Turn off" key.
goveeError.network: This PC is not connected to a local network: the Govee lights cannot be reached.
action.media.hint: The keyboard's media keys: play, pause, next track, Windows volume, and the whole PC's microphone. Works with Spotify, YouTube, Deezer…, even in the background.
action.keys.hint: Presses a key combination for you (Ctrl + C, Win + Shift + S…), in the window you opened the deck over.
action.text.hint: Pastes a ready-made text into the window you opened the deck over (the chat, Discord…). Your clipboard is put back right after.
field.micMuteHint: Mutes every microphone of the PC at once, for every app: Discord, OBS, Teams, games… Like the mute button of Windows' sound settings. The key shows “Muted” while they are off.
field.keysCapture: Click here, then press the keys
field.keysHint: Ctrl, Alt, Shift and Win add or remove a key: Windows keeps most Win + … shortcuts for itself, they can't be recorded from the keyboard.
field.textEnter: Press Enter after it (sends the message)
keyboardError.badCombo: This button is not set up: choose the keys to send.
keyboardError.badMedia: This button is not set up: choose a media key.
keyboardError.emptyText: This button is not set up: write the text to paste.
keyboardError.blocked: Windows blocked the keys sent: try again.
micError.noMic: No microphone found: check that it is plugged in.
library.title: Template library
library.subtitle: Ready-made decks, added in one click. Each one goes on a new page: your buttons stay where they are, and you can change everything afterwards.
library.emptyPage: Empty page: start from a ready-made template.
library.added: Template “{name}” added on a new page.
library.todo: {count} button(s) to complete: click them to finish setting them up.
library.connectFirst: Connect {software} so the scenes and the microphone fill in by themselves.
library.noRoom: The deck already has {max} pages, the maximum: delete a page to add this template.
tpl.stream.name: Stream essentials
tpl.stream.description: 4 scenes, live, recording, clip and microphone. With OBS or Streamlabs connected, the buttons pick up your scenes and microphone by themselves.
tpl.chat.name: Chat messages
tpl.chat.description: Ready-made messages, pasted into the chat and sent: thanks, welcome, break… Click in the chat, then open the deck.
tpl.chat.thanksText: Thanks for the support, you're awesome! ✨
tpl.chat.discordText: Join the Discord: (put your link here)
tpl.discord.name: Discord
tpl.discord.description: Mute the microphone, deafen and open Discord. In Discord › Settings › Keybinds, set Ctrl + Shift + M to mute and Ctrl + Shift + D to deafen: they then work even with Discord in the background.
tpl.music.name: Music and video
tpl.music.description: Play, pause, next track and Windows volume. Works with Spotify, Deezer, YouTube and most players, even with the deck closed.
tpl.windows.name: Windows shortcuts
tpl.windows.description: Copy, paste, screenshot, desktop, File Explorer… The shortcuts go to the window you opened the deck over.
tpl.browser.name: Browser
tpl.browser.description: Tabs, reload, back, full screen and find, for Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Opera.
tpl.teams.name: Teams meeting
tpl.teams.description: Microphone, camera, raise hand, share screen and hang up, with Microsoft Teams shortcuts. Open the deck over the meeting.
tpl.zoom.name: Zoom meeting
tpl.zoom.description: Microphone, camera, raise hand, share screen, record and leave, with Zoom shortcuts. Open the deck over the meeting.
